clinician.trajectory_summary: A 24-year-old woman with no significant past medical history presented to dermatology with two painful, progressively enlarging papules in the left auricular region: a posterior auricular papule present for 8 months and a preauricular papule present for 4 months. Shave biopsy of both lesions was performed, revealing histopathological findings characteristic of epithelioid hemangioendothelioma: cellular dermal proliferations of epithelioid cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm arranged in cords within a myxohyaline stroma, with subtle intracytoplasmic vacuoles containing red blood cells. Histological and immunohistochemical findings confirmed the EHE diagnosis. Subsequent staging with CT scans of the head, neck, chest, abdomen, and pelvis revealed metastatic disease, including innumerable bilateral pulmonary nodules, a 1.8-cm hypoattenuated hepatic lesion, and prominent bilateral axillary lymph nodes. After oncologic consultation, the patient elected a watchful waiting approach with serial CT scans recommended every 3 months to monitor disease progression.
